source.check: returned without a contest: 'Downpatrick Rural Council will show only one change' (Kilmore) and 'There will be no contests' (Belfast News-Letter, 7 May 1936, p. 15); appointed a council representative on the Ulster Tourist Development Association at the annual meeting, 10 June 1936 (round 2, 7 Nov 2026)

note: Triennial election of the Downpatrick rural district council, 1936; polling day for Co. Down, Thursday 4 June 1936. There were no contests and only one change, at Kilmore (Belfast News-Letter, 7 May 1936, p. 15). The unchanged divisions are not named. Four more divisions (Dunmore, Killinchy, Killyleagh Rural, Strangford) are recorded from the report of the new council's annual meeting on 10 June 1936, each with its division from the 1930 return, and Castlewellan Rural from the report of its member's resignation in July 1936, when Joseph M'Sherry was co-opted in his place (round 2, 7 Nov 2026). division inferred from the 3 May 1930 return (S. Sharvin, Strangford); the council-meeting report cited names the member as sitting within six months of the election. Returned unopposed.
